category: Category A — General Conversational and Domain Tests
name: Mixed legal and unrelated question
expected: Addresses the unpaid salary legal issue thoroughly; politely redirects the movie suggestion request as out of scope.
prompt: My employer has not paid me. Also, suggest a movie.
raw_response:
Hello! I understand how stressful it is when your employer fails to pay your earned wages, but I cannot suggest a movie because I specialize exclusively in Indian legal matters.

### | Your Situation
An employer has withheld your unpaid salary without providing timely payment for work completed. The key issue involves wage non-payment and financial recovery under Indian employment laws.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under Section 5 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the last day of the wage period (or the 10th day if more than 1,000 persons are employed).
- Under Section 7 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, any arbitrary, unauthorized, or unexplained withholding of your salary is illegal, as deductions can only be made for specifically permitted reasons.
- Under Section 15 of The Payment of Wages Act, 1936, you have the statutory right to approach the designated Authority to claim delayed or unpaid wages, which includes seeking compensation up to ten times the amount unlawfully withheld.
- Under Section 73 of The Indian Contract Act, 1872, you are entitled to claim compensation for loss or damage caused by the breach of your employment contract.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence such as your employment contract, appointment letter, salary slips, bank statements, and any written communication or emails requesting your unpaid wages.
2. Send a formal written demand notice to your employer demanding the release of your full unpaid salary and granting a clear period of 15 days to comply.
3. Approach the appropriate forum, such as filing an application before the designated Labour Commissioner or Authority under the Payment of Wages Act if the employer fails to settle your dues.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
What is your total unpaid salary amount and how many months of wages are currently pending from your employer?

citations.title: Time of payment of wages and Claims arising out of deductions from wages or delay in payment
citations.description: Wages must be paid before the expiry of the 7th day after the wage period (or 10th day if more than 1,000 persons employed). Section 15 provides for application to the designated Authority for delayed wages with compensation up to ten times the amount deducted/delayed.

citations.title: Deductions which may be made from wages
citations.description: Strictly enumerates permissible deductions (such as authorized provident fund, income tax, or willful damage shown after formal inquiry). Any arbitrary or unauthorized deduction is unlawful.

citations.section: Settlement of Dues and Service Conditions Provision
citations.title: Statutory Payment of Earned Salary and Notice Pay for Private/Commercial Employees
citations.description: State-specific legislation (e.g., Delhi Shops Act, Karnataka Shops & Commercial Establishments Act, Maharashtra Shops Act) governing commercial and IT/office establishments. Mandates clearance of earned wages and final settlement upon termination or resignation within 3 to 15 days.

citations.title: Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract
citations.description: When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive, from the party who has broken the contract, compensation for any loss or damage caused to him thereby.
